newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $20 a tonne higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $20 a tonne higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $20 a tonne higher Monday as traders expect the market to bounce back after sliding nine percent in the past three trading sessions.
CSCE was closed Friday in observance of U.S. Independence Day.
Thursday, New York cocoa futures fell sharply for the third day in a row, with September sliding $52 to end at $1,562 amid heavy selling on the part of commodity funds.
Technically, September resistance was pegged at $1,580, followed by $1,600. Support was seen at $1,514, a low from mid-June.
On the fundamental side, the second quarter U.K. and Dutch grindings released on Friday were within expectations, traders said.
U.K. second quarter 1997 grinds fell 4.1 percent to 42,702 tonnes compared to the same period in 1996. Expectations were for a flat to slightly lower second quarter grind.
In the Netherlands, grindings rose by a higher-than-expected 10.4 percent compared with the second quarter of 1996, to 100,132 tonnes. Analysts had expected a modest rise.
London cocoa futures were trading higher early Monday, buoyed by light trade buying. At the midday break, LIFFE September rose nine stg, to 1,047 stg, after peaking at 1,052 stg.
